features.summary: Event bus: the simulation emits events (notices, refresh, bell, crisis, voyage end) and each game's UI subscribes, so game logic never touches the screen.
outputs: synchronous calls to every handler added with EV.on(type, fn)
features.adaptation: Any game: subscribe its own UI to the same event names. A blimp game could show 'say' notices as a radio log instead of toasts.

features.summary: Player options the simulation asks about (assists, automatic helpers, is a dialog open) without reading the page.
inputs: OPT.def(id, fn) and OPT.use(fallback) from the game
features.adaptation: Any game: answer the same ids from its own settings screen, or from fixed values for a game with no assists.

features.summary: Seedable random numbers: mulberry32 streams, the simulation stream rng, normal deviates and text hashing for repeatable seeds.
The live game state S, the sim clock (speedMult, paused), the longest simulation step and a time-of-day formatter.
features.adaptation: Game-neutral; a faster vehicle may want a shorter MAXSTEP.

features.summary: Turns game state into text and back (Sets and infinities survive) and shrinks big saves by thinning long tracks and trimming logs.
features.adaptation: Game-neutral; each game picks its own arrays to thin and where the text is stored.

features.summary: Wind at any point and time: a wandering prevailing wind with a daily rhythm, squalls and passing systems on top, bent by land (blocking, venturi round points and through passages, long lee shadows behind high ground, sea and land breezes, afternoon gusts).
inputs: world state s (s.wx systems, s.wx.cover, s.squall)
optional altitude alt (m above the surface)
FIELD.localHour(s,t), FIELD.land() {I:land masses, P:passages}, FIELD.hold() test holds
outputs: windAt -> {from (deg), kn, lee (land name), pass (passage name), breeze ('sea breeze'/'land breeze')}
features.adaptation: Blimp or glider: pass alt in metres; wind strengthens with height (Hellmann shear) and land blocking and lee shadows fade as the craft climbs toward peak height. Give FIELD.land() hills or mountains with heights; set WIND_BASE to the region's prevailing wind. A land vehicle could use it for dust, sail-cart or fire spread.

features.summary: Weather systems drawn ahead of time (surges, lulls, tropical waves, cold fronts) plus squalls; they drive wind-sea and swell, rain, lightning, cloud cover and darkness, and a barometer that falls before the big ones, with notices emitted as events.
inputs: wxStep(s,dt,w): step in hours and the local wind
outputs: s.wx {ev, sea {dir, amp, swF, swA}, H wave height m, rain, cover, dark, flash, bolt}
EV 'wx' events: wave1-3, front1-3, surge, lull, squallNear, shift {dd, from}
features.adaptation: Blimp: ignore sea and swell, use rain, cloud, squalls and the falling glass as flying hazards (turbulence from squall boost, icing under cover). A desert game could swap waves and fronts for sandstorms by changing event types and their wind effect.

features.summary: Dead reckoning: the reckoned position and its growing error from ordered course and logged speed, log readings, a noon sight for latitude, bearings on landmarks with weather-dependent noise, a cross-bearing fix, and a least-squares mark position that bends the track.
inputs: navReckon(s,ordered,dt): course in degrees and step in hours
state s.est, s.estSpeed, s.estTrack, s.bearings, s.noon
outputs: s.estTrack, s.marks, s.latLines, s.fixes, s.sights, s.heaves
EV 'navBearing', 'navNoon', 'navFix', 'navMark' events with the numbers for the game to word
knobs: MARK_SPEED_FRESH (how recent a log counts as fresh)
bearing spread given by the game
features.adaptation: Blimp: the speed log becomes an airspeed or ground-speed reading, bearings are on peaks, towns or radio beacons, and the noon sight still gives latitude; wind drift can be left hidden from the reckoning as currents are for ships. Any vehicle without GPS can reuse it unchanged.

features.summary: A crew of individuals with roles, skill, temper, spirits and health, three watches with fatigue and sleep, rations and scurvy, fever and injury with a surgeon, hiring and paying off in port, shore leave, discipline, and crisis moments (man overboard, fire, mutiny, surgery) offered as choice cards.
inputs: crewStep(s,dt,w): step in hours and the wind {kn}
crewMake(spec): named hands, seamen names, berth order, doctors
hireList(s) / hireHand(id) / payOff(m) / shoreLeave() / issueRum() / punish(m)
crewRota(C) / crewBosunWatch(C): even out the watches
CREWG hooks: localHours, dayIndex, atPort, modalOpen, skipping, money, maxCrew, minCrew, effN, role, dutyRate, berths, berthOwner, watchNames, names
state s.crew, s.stores, s.ration, s.wx, s.squall
outputs: s.crew fields (mode, f fatigue, mo spirits, sk skill, hp, scv, fev, sick), s.eff work output, s.fat, s.helmN, s.helmF
EV 'crewRemoved' (man, index), 'crewHired' (man), 'crewBill', 'crisis' (card with options) and 'say' notices
features.adaptation: Blimp: the roster becomes aircrew and riggers with the same fatigue, watches and morale; scurvy becomes any long-trip condition (oxygen, cold) by renaming; man overboard becomes a fall from the gondola; roles, berths and names come from the game's data through the CREWG hooks.

features.summary: Guided lesson runner: a lesson is a list of steps, each with a done test on the game state; it advances, flags a stuck player and ends, and the game draws the card and highlight.
inputs: a lesson {id, stuckMs, steps[{id, title, text, hint, target, ready, done, enter}]}
tutStart, tutStep(now) called a few times a second
outputs: state s.tut {id, i, f, stuck, done, skipped}
features.adaptation: Any game: write its own lesson as steps that test its own state (a blimp: cast off, climb to 500 ft, trim the burner, read the drift). Only the words, targets and card are new.
